Entry: Today's the day! Maya and I, as Joya, have officially started our gap year adventure. We landed at Incheon International Airport and took the train to our lodging near Bukchon Hanok Village in Jongno-gu, Seoul. I already love the mix of old and new—traditional Korean houses surrounded by the modern city. We settled into our traditional guesthouse and got a good night's rest after the long journey.

We spent most of the day exploring the area right around our guesthouse in Bukchon Hanok Village. The area is stunning, full of beautifully preserved hanok houses. We walked the charming, hilly streets, admiring the architecture and found a cozy spot for a coffee and some light shopping. We decided to take it easy today to get over the jet lag and are excited for tomorrow's palace visits.

Our day was packed with culture! We visited one of Seoul's grand palaces, likely Gyeongbokgung or Changdeokgung, marveling at the intricate details and vast courtyards. It's incredible to see such ancient beauty preserved right in the middle of a massive metropolis. The modern skyline peeking over the traditional walls makes for such a cool contrast! We took a break for a small meal and some relaxation back at our traditional guesthouse near the hanok village.

We ventured out for more sightseeing. After a slow start at our guesthouse, we dove deeper into Korean history, visiting a major history museum to get more context for the palaces we'd seen. It was fascinating to learn about the Joseon Dynasty and the country's transformation. We ended the evening near our lodging, grabbing a delicious meal and picking up a few snacks for tomorrow.

Food, glorious food! We spent the morning near Gangnam, taking the subway to get there. It was a whirlwind of modern commerce, totally different from the historical area we're staying in. In the evening, we were back in the Jongno area, fully immersing ourselves in the local food scene. We tried authentic Korean BBQ—the sizzling meat was heavenly! We also explored the bustling street food in Myeong-dong, indulging in corn dogs, mandu, and fried chicken. We capped the night off with a relaxing drink and snack back near Bukchon.

Today we got a great view of the city's nature. We walked around Namsan Park, enjoying the late autumn scenery and the views of the N Seoul Tower. We did some retail therapy and found a great little café for a midday break in the Myeong-dong area. After a full day out, we got dinner and some items near our guesthouse, ready for another day of exploration.

We dedicated today to a somber but important cultural stop: the Odusan Unification Observation Deck. It offered a stark, moving view of the divided Korean peninsula. It was a very impactful visit, providing a lot of perspective on the country's recent history. The rest of the day was spent quietly near our accommodation, reflecting on the experience and planning the final days of our time in Seoul.

A quieter day today as we prepared for our change of scenery. We enjoyed the last few peaceful moments in our traditional guesthouse in Bukchon Hanok Village. We spent time relaxing and getting reorganized before relocating to a new part of Seoul for one last night in the capital tomorrow.

We moved from our guesthouse in Jongno to a different lodging in a new area of Seoul, near Sinsang-dong, to explore more before heading to Jeonju. We spent the day soaking up the city's atmosphere, grabbing a flavorful bibimbap for lunch—one of our favorite Korean dishes! In the evening, we were out enjoying the bustling atmosphere and grabbing one last street food fix before our train ride tomorrow.

We took a morning train from Seoul down to Jeonju, the birthplace of bibimbap! The pace here is already slower and so refreshing. We checked into our accommodation right within the Jeonju Hanok Village, a charming area with over 800 traditional houses. We immediately headed out to find the original bibimbap place for dinner—it was unbelievable, truly the best we’ve ever had. We also visited a local museum near the village to get a taste of local history and culture.

Jeonju is living up to its 'Slow City' designation. The Hanok Village here is vast, and we loved just wandering the streets. We spent a lot of time exploring the area around the village, including the local restaurants and cultural centers. In the evening, we took another walk through the village, enjoying the peaceful atmosphere and the beautifully lit traditional homes.

We had a more structured day, visiting a nearby local store and then heading back to the heart of the Hanok Village. We stopped for some coffee and enjoyed another quiet meal, probably dak galbi, which we’ve grown to love! The slower pace here is just what we needed after the hustle of Seoul. We even found a small food spot near the village for some local snacks.

Our last full day in Jeonju was dedicated to soaking up the traditional culture. We visited the Gyeonggijeon Shrine, home to the portrait of the founder of the Joseon Dynasty, and enjoyed a walk to the Omokdae outlook for a panoramic view of the hanok village. For dinner, we had to get one last taste of authentic Jeonju food before preparing to head to Busan tomorrow.

We left our peaceful hanok in Jeonju today and took the train to the vibrant port city of Busan. The change of scenery is dramatic—from serene traditional houses to a bustling coastal metropolis. We checked into our lodging and took an evening stroll to get a sense of the city, excited for all the ocean activities planned for the coming days.

The coast is calling! We started our Busan exploration with the Songdo Marine Cable Car, getting stunning aerial views of the coastline and the Songdo beach. Afterwards, we headed to the colorful, artistic Gamcheon Culture Village—it felt like walking through a massive, open-air art gallery clinging to the hillside. The views from there were fantastic.

Today was all about the ocean and local life. We visited the bustling Jagalchi Fish Market, an explosion for the senses with all the fresh seafood. For lunch, we had some fantastic, fresh seafood right there at the market. Later, we visited the Oryukdo Islets, a chain of small islands, which offered incredible natural beauty and a nice walk along the coast.

We took a full-day excursion to Gyeongju, the historic capital of the ancient Silla Kingdom. It was like stepping back in time—an incredible concentration of temples, royal tombs, and cultural relics. We visited Bulguksa Temple and the Cheomseongdae Observatory. It was a long day, but worth it to experience such a crucial part of Korean history, making us appreciate the depth of the country's heritage.

After our day trip, we enjoyed a slightly slower day back in Busan. We explored more of the local neighborhoods, found a great place for some Dak Galbi, and did some light souvenir shopping. It was a good day to recharge and enjoy the modern, lively atmosphere of Busan.

We spent the day near the beach, perhaps Haeundae or Gwangalli, enjoying the last of the Korean seaside views. We walked along the sand and enjoyed the city's architecture and ocean air. We found a great spot for dinner to try some more of the local Busan specialties.

Our final full day in South Korea! We packed up most of our things and spent the remaining time savoring the atmosphere in Busan. We had one last big Korean meal, reminiscing about all the amazing food we've had, from Seoul's street food to Jeonju's bibimbap and Busan's fresh seafood. It's been an unforgettable first stop on our gap year.

Time to say goodbye to Korea! We hopped on a morning flight from Busan to Osaka, Japan. It was a quick and easy transition, and now we’re in a new country and a new adventure begins. I'm excited to see the sights and, of course, try the famous Japanese food. Korea was an incredible mix of history, nature, and ultra-modern city life. Next stop: Japan!

We finally arrived in Osaka, Japan, from Busan, South Korea! We checked into our hotel and immediately set out to explore the neighborhood. We ended up in Dotonbori, which is even more vibrant and dazzling than the pictures. The energy is incredible, and we just had to try some street food. It was the perfect welcome to Japan. I have a feeling we'll be spending a lot of time here.

Today was a deep dive into Osaka's history. We started at the majestic Osaka Castle, which is absolutely stunning. Walking through the grounds and the main tower gave us a great sense of the city's past. We continued our history lesson at the Osaka Museum of History and then had a somber but important visit to Peace Osaka, the city's museum dedicated to World War II. For dinner, we went back to Dotonbori for more delicious street snacks and I discovered my new obsession: Japanese curry. It’s so rich and flavorful!

We spent the morning exploring the unique atmosphere of Den Den Town, the 'Electric Town' of Osaka, which was a lot of fun with all the anime and electronics shops. Then we went to Shinsekai, the 'New World,' which has a retro, old-Osaka feel. We went up the Tsutenkaku Tower for panoramic views of the city. The evening was magical; we went to Tennoji Park, and they had a wonderful Christmas celebration going on. The lights and festive spirit were lovely.

What a beautiful day! We visited the Sumiyoshi Taisha Grand Shrine, one of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines. Its unique architecture, particularly the *Sumi-yoshi-zukuri* style, was fascinating to see. Later in the day, we absolutely indulged at a Ramenfest. There were so many different types of ramen to try—a true feast! I'm officially hooked on Japanese food; the savory broth and tender noodles were perfection. We even had some amazing gyoza on the side.

Today was a lovely, unplanned day just soaking up the atmosphere of Osaka. We wandered through different local neighborhoods, stumbled upon some charming small shops, and enjoyed a slower pace. I spent the afternoon perfecting my onigiri-eating technique—they are the perfect snack! Of course, we ended the evening with a final stop at Dotonbori for dinner and to see the famous Glico Running Man sign lit up.

We took a day trip to Himeji today, and it was so worth it! We visited the magnificent Himeji Castle, known as the 'White Heron Castle.' It is one of Japan’s most beautiful original castles and looks incredible against the sky. But the real highlight was Koko-en Garden right next to it. The nine separate traditional Japanese gardens were breathtaking, especially the incredible water features. We capped off the visit with a peaceful and traditional tea ceremony in the garden. A perfect day.

Kobe day trip! This day will go down in history. We took the funicular up to the top of Mount Maya and were rewarded with a spectacular view, often called the '10-Million Dollar Night View,' overlooking Kobe and Osaka. It was chilly, so we enjoyed a warm wine while taking it all in. Then came the food experience of a lifetime: we had Kobe A5 wagyu beef. I can honestly say it was the single best piece of food either of us has ever put in our mouths. It melted like butter—an absolute culinary dream.

Today was all about a day trip to Nara, the old capital. The deer there are considered sacred, and they roam freely in Nara Park, bowing to you for crackers! It was such a unique and charming experience. We also visited Todai-ji Temple, which houses the enormous *Daibutsu*, or Big Buddha statue. The sheer scale of the wooden temple and the statue inside was awe-inspiring. It was a wonderful day of nature, history, and adorable deer.

We checked out of our Osaka hotel this morning and took the train to Kyoto! We got settled in and immediately went out to the Kyoto Botanical Garden. We spent the afternoon doing *momijigari*, which is the beautiful Japanese tradition of hunting for the most perfect autumn colors. The vibrant reds and golds were stunning. For dinner, Maya found her new favorite gyoza at Gyoza Hohei near the Takashimaya department store. She says it’s the best she’s ever had!

What an incredible cultural day! We rented beautiful kimonos and spent the whole day walking around in them, which made us feel like we had stepped back in time. We started with another wonderful traditional tea ceremony, a truly peaceful experience. Then we explored the historic Gion district, Kyoto’s famous geisha quarter, all while dressed in our kimonos. It was magical to walk those cobblestone streets and feel so immersed in Japanese tradition.

We took a trip out to the Arashiyama area today. It's famous for its stunning bamboo forest, which was so quiet and tranquil as we walked through the towering stalks. Later, we visited a unique ninja and samurai museum. It was really fun and interactive; we learned a lot about the history and techniques of these legendary Japanese warriors. A perfect blend of nature and historical adventure.

Fushimi Inari Taisha was absolutely incredible! Walking through the thousands of vibrant red-orange *torii* gates that wind up the mountain was a breathtaking experience. After that, we hopped on the train to Uji, a town famous for its high-quality matcha green tea. We sampled some of the best matcha I've ever tasted right at the source. While there, we also visited the beautiful Byodo-in Temple, also known as the Phoenix Hall. It was a lovely, nature-filled day.

Today was mostly a travel day as we made our way from Kyoto to Kaga, preparing for a special stay tomorrow. We checked into our hotel—an APA Hotel—which we’ve already decided is our new favorite Japanese hotel chain. It’s simple, clean, and always has everything you need. After the long train ride, we just relaxed and enjoyed a simple, cozy night in Kaga.

Pure bliss! Today we arrived at Beniya Mukayu, a beautiful, tranquil *ryokan* (traditional inn). It's located in the mountains and is known for its incredible hospitality and relaxing atmosphere. The experience was one of the most relaxing we've ever had. Everything from the traditional multi-course dinner to soaking in the private hot spring bath was perfect. This stay is an absolute 10/10; we'll definitely do this again.

After reluctantly leaving our *ryokan*, we traveled to Kanazawa. After settling in, we went straight to explore Kanazawa Castle. The castle park and the reconstructed buildings are beautiful, and we enjoyed learning about the Maeda clan, who ruled this area. The city has a wonderful, refined atmosphere. We ended the day with a delicious dinner, still thinking about that amazing Japanese curry.

We visited the magnificent Kenroku-en Garden today, which is considered one of the 'Three Great Gardens of Japan.' It truly lives up to the reputation—it's absolutely stunning. The vast, meticulously maintained grounds with their ponds, hills, and tea houses were so serene. It was the perfect place to stroll and enjoy the tranquility and beauty of nature.

Our last full day in Japan, and we spent it exploring the historic districts of Kanazawa, specifically the *chaya* or geisha districts. We walked through the beautifully preserved wooden architecture of Higashi Chaya, the largest and most famous district. The area has such an old-world charm. It was a lovely, low-key way to conclude our sightseeing in Japan.

We finally arrived in Bangkok, Thailand, from Kanazawa! The journey felt a little long, but getting settled into our apartment in the city felt instantly relaxing. The plan is to take it easy for a few days to really soak in the change of pace and prepare for more intensive sightseeing later on. It’s nice just to have a comfortable place to call home for a bit.

Today, we ventured out to the nearby Emsphere shopping center to get a feel for the modern side of Bangkok life. I wasn't expecting a life-changing culinary experience in a mall, but wow, was I wrong! We tried the pad thai from Padthai Chapaa, and it was absolutely the best I've ever had. It's supposed to be made by a genuine master, and I believe it—the flavors were incredible. I'm already thinking about when we can go back for more of that perfect noodle dish.

Another wonderfully low-key day. We spent most of the time just enjoying the comfort of our apartment in Bangkok. We did a little local food run later in the day, exploring some nearby options. It's such a nice change of pace to just wander and pick up street food or a casual meal without a set plan. This relaxation is just what we needed before diving into the major tourist sites.

Merry Christmas from Bangkok! We celebrated today by calling our families to wish them happy holidays, which was a lovely way to feel connected despite the distance. For our own celebration, we decided on a perfect meal: we went back to Emsphere just for another round of that amazing pad thai from Padthai Chapaa. It’s becoming a new holiday tradition! It was just as delicious the second time, and it was a simple, wonderful way to spend Christmas together.

We made the move today to a new place closer to the historic center of Bangkok, in the lively Chinatown area. We immediately set out for the major sights, starting with the Grand Palace. It was absolutely stunning! The sheer scale and intricate golden detail of the complex, especially the buildings like the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, were breathtaking. Right nearby, we also visited the incredible Wat Pho, famous for the colossal Reclining Buddha. The sheer size of the gold-plated statue was astounding. Today was a perfect mix of magnificent architecture, powerful religious sites, and a great start to our city adventures.

John and I spent our day exploring the historic Thonburi side of Bangkok. We started at the magnificent Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, admiring its stunning prang. Later, we visited a beautiful place of worship close by, which I believe was Wat Intharawihan, home to a massive standing Buddha statue. For lunch, we enjoyed some local food in the area before heading back.

Today was a day for practicalities and local life in Bangkok. We used the transit system quite a bit to move around the Krung Thep Maha Nakhon area. We did some shopping at a store and made sure to try some delicious street food around the Silom area. The public transport hubs make navigating the city so much easier!

We had a big day of sightseeing and culture in Bangkok! We started with a walk through Lumphini Park, the green heart of the city, before heading over to a museum, likely the nearby Jim Thompson House, which was fascinating. We found a great spot for lunch and, later, a couple of lovely cafes for a break. We also made sure to pick up some new clothes. Our evening ended with some drinks at a local bar.

Today was a big travel day. We started in Bangkok, where we visited a beautiful marble-clad place of worship, which I suspect was Wat Benchamabophit, before doing some final quick shopping. In the afternoon, we flew out of Suvarnabhumi Airport and landed in Chiang Mai. I’m so excited for the northern part of our trip!

Happy New Year’s Eve! We spent the day exploring the temples within Chiang Mai's Old City. We paid our respects at the impressive Wat Chedi Luang and the beautiful Wat Phra Singh. We did a little shopping, grabbed a snack from a bakery, and ended the year with a tasty dinner, enjoying the local Chiang Mai cuisine.

We started the New Year right here in Chiang Mai! We took care of some chores, dropping off our laundry, and then spent time wandering and doing a bit of browsing at some local stores. Of course, a travel day isn't complete without trying some great local food, which we made sure to do today.
A quieter day today in Chiang Mai. We did some more errands, including a couple of trips to the store and getting more laundry done. It’s important to take care of the essentials even when exploring!

We had a truly memorable day of exploring outside Chiang Mai. We drove south to the stunning Doi Inthanon National Park, the 'Roof of Thailand,' to see the beautiful pagodas near the summit. Later, back in the city, we visited a cafe, did a bit of last-minute shopping at some nearby stores, grabbed dinner, and enjoyed the lively nightlife at a bar before turning in.

Another travel day! We started with our morning routine in Chiang Mai, taking care of laundry and some shopping. Then, we made our way to Chiang Rai. After checking into our accommodation, we visited a restaurant for a meal and took a pleasant walk in the city park. We also stopped by an electronics store, maybe for a new gadget!

Chiang Rai captivated us with its temples today! We took a trip out of the city center to visit the incredibly unique Wat Rong Khun, the White Temple. Later, we visited another beautiful place of worship, likely Wat Phra Kaeo, which is famous for its association with the Emerald Buddha. We also managed to fit in some local food and a little bit of souvenir shopping.

We moved on from Chiang Rai, stopping briefly at a store before making our way south to Phayao. After settling into our new lodging, we took a walk around the area near our campground, preparing for tomorrow's exploration of this quieter region.

Phayao proved to be a lovely, serene stop. We started the morning with coffee at a local cafe and then visited the impressive Wat Si Khom Kham on the shores of Phayao Lake, home to a massive Buddha statue. After our spiritual morning, we traveled back north to Chiang Rai, had dinner at a restaurant, and enjoyed the evening at a bar near our accommodation.

It was another whirlwind day of travel! We had a quick stop at a cafe near our lodging in Chiang Rai before heading to the airport. We flew from Chiang Rai, had a brief layover in Bangkok, where we managed to do some shopping, and then took a final flight all the way down to the tropical island of Phuket. We grabbed a quick beauty treatment after landing before settling in for the night.
Our first full day in Phuket was all about the famous Patong Beach area. We spent most of the evening exploring the lively nightlife and atmosphere, enjoying a few drinks at local bars.

We had a busy day on Phuket! We started with some errands, including a quick stop near a doctor's office, before indulging in the local food and some more beauty treatments. Later in the day, we took a domestic flight out of Phuket and traveled to Surat Thani, landing near Koh Samui to enjoy some time at a spa.

Today was a day of total relaxation on Koh Phangan! John and I spent hours at a fantastic spa, getting multiple treatments. It was exactly what we needed to unwind and fully embrace the island pace. The tranquil setting was perfect. We basically just enjoyed the serenity and the pampering all day. I already feel so refreshed.

We decided to venture out from our spa sanctuary a bit today on Koh Phangan. We started the day by finding some delicious local Thai food for breakfast, which was an incredible start. Later, we did a little souvenir shopping and even stopped by a chill bar for a quick drink to watch some of the island life go by. We ended up back at the wonderful spa for more treatments in the late afternoon and evening, because you can never have too much pampering, right? I'm loving the food scene here in Surat Thani province.

We decided to move lodging today on Koh Phangan, which took us to a new hotel near the port. Before settling into the new place, we had an early morning spa session, because John and I are getting addicted to how relaxing it is! We stopped by a travel agency to start planning our next leg of the trip—so many beautiful islands to choose from. After getting set up at the hotel, we spent the afternoon with another spa visit. For dinner, we had a lovely meal at a nearby restaurant, making sure to try more authentic Thai dishes. The food has been amazing.

I think we may have broken a record for spa time! We had a few quick spa visits and some food in the early hours of the morning on Koh Phangan. Then, we headed out for a late breakfast at a great restaurant near the pier. We're getting ready to leave the island and this little ritual of food and relaxation is the perfect send-off. The local food is just so flavorful.

We woke up in Surat Thani province on the mainland today and had a nice, early breakfast. Our big activity for the day was visiting the Bandon International Temple, a beautiful tourist attraction with stunning architecture and a serene atmosphere. We love seeing these unique cultural and religious sites. It was a lovely day spent admiring the sights and soaking up the culture.

Today was a travel day! We were still in Surat Thani this morning, where we made a stop at an ATM before catching our transportation at the local transit station, likely a bus or train, to head towards Krabi. The journey was scenic. Once we arrived in the Krabi area, we checked in and immediately went for some classic Thai massage at a spa. To cap off the day, we had a delicious dinner at a restaurant in Ao Nang, near the beach. I think we’re going to love exploring the beautiful limestone karsts and beaches here!

Today was a travel day that started in Thailand! John and I grabbed a final, delicious meal in Krabi Town, close to where the bustling night market is. It seems we also had a quick stop at a health facility nearby before heading to Krabi International Airport. We had to return our rental car before checking in for our flight. Next thing I knew, we landed at Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Selangor, Malaysia. It was a long journey, but we made it to our next country!

We didn't do much today except settle into Kuala Lumpur. The one entry I see for the day shows us near a transit station in the city center. I bet we were taking the train to our accommodation after arriving late yesterday. It's nice to finally be here and feel the pulse of this huge city.

We spent a lot of time exploring Kuala Lumpur today, mostly using the excellent transit system, including a stop near the Batu Caves station early in the day. We seemed to visit a health facility and had a lovely meal in the Mont Kiara area. Then it was back downtown where we did quite a bit of shopping, with several stops near the famous Petronas Twin Towers. We walked through one of the large shopping centers, maybe Suria KLCC, before ending our day back near a transit hub.

What a day for sightseeing! We started by taking the train near the Merdeka Square area. We spent some time right by the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and the City Gallery, soaking up the history and beautiful architecture of this colonial-era center. I recall the area was full of impressive landmarks. It looks like we also stopped at a health center not too far from there. It's great how accessible everything is here!

Our last full day in Kuala Lumpur was a mix of relaxation and exploration. We were near the famous Petaling Street market, exploring the colorful shops, grabbing a coffee at a cafe, and having a nice meal. We must have been picking up a souvenir since we were at a florist near there as well! We also visited a beautiful place of worship, likely a historic temple or mosque in the old city center, before grabbing some last-minute food and heading back to our place. It’s been a fantastic trip to Malaysia.

What a whirlwind travel day! John and I started the day in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, taking a train before heading to the airport. We had time for a quick meal and a drink at a bar right by the gate at Kuala Lumpur International Airport before our flight. It was a long travel day, but we finally landed in Kerala, India! We grabbed some local food near the Cochin International Airport late in the evening before settling in for the night.

We spent our first full day exploring the charming, historic area of Fort Kochi. We're staying at a lovely lodging nearby, and the whole area is just steeped in history. We did a bit of shopping at some local clothing stores and markets in the morning, which was fun. For lunch, we enjoyed a delicious meal at a restaurant in the area, likely sampling some of the wonderful seafood Fort Kochi is known for. The food is incredible so far!

Another day immersed in the local markets of Fort Kochi! We were right back at the shops, picking up souvenirs and enjoying the local atmosphere. It was nice to take a relaxed morning, wandering through the different stores and seeing all the beautiful, colorful textiles and other goods. Fort Kochi has such a unique vibe.

Time to move on from Fort Kochi. We traveled to another part of Kerala, taking a flight from what seems to be a smaller regional airport in the area, possibly near the mountainous region of Munnar, famous for its tea plantations. We're excited for the next leg of our journey.

Today brought us to the famous backwaters of Alleppey! We checked into a wonderful lodging right on the water. The serene canals and lush greenery are exactly as beautiful as I'd imagined. It's the perfect place to experience the unique nature and peaceful life of Kerala's backwaters.

After an early start and a little more local shopping in Alleppey, we said goodbye to Kerala and flew up north. We arrived in Gujarat, and celebrated our arrival with a fantastic dinner at a restaurant in the Ahmedabad area. It's a huge contrast to the south, and I'm looking forward to exploring this new region.

We've made it to Jaipur, Rajasthan, and the fun is really starting! We checked into our beautiful hotel, which has an old heritage feel, and then met up with John's long-time friend Ram and his fiancé, Mekhala. I know John was really looking forward to seeing them. We spent the day catching up and exploring the area near our hotel. The location seems to be near a lot of different professional offices, which is interesting.

Ram and Mekhala showed us around Jaipur today! We started near our hotel, running some small errands. Then, we made use of the Jaipur Metro system to get around, which was convenient. We stopped at a few local stores, picked up some fuel for the car, and then visited a large green space, maybe a local park, in the northern part of the city. We also got to see a beautiful place of worship, a temple, in the area, which was lovely.

Another day in Jaipur, and we enjoyed a relaxed morning at our hotel. We did some more local shopping before heading out with Ram and Mekhala. We visited a prominent Hindu temple in the city, the Govind Dev Ji Temple, which is a central part of the city's spiritual life. We also did some last-minute shopping at local stores. The architecture in the 'Pink City' is really something else.

Happy Birthday to John! What an unforgettable way to celebrate! We traveled to Agra, Uttar Pradesh, and spent the day at the magnificent Taj Mahal. It truly is one of the most incredible sights I have ever seen—a stunning monument of love and an architectural masterpiece. We also managed to squeeze in a lovely birthday lunch nearby. A perfect day for a perfect person.

We left Agra this morning after having a meal near our lodging, and then we were on our way to New Delhi. We stopped for a quick bite near the highway on the way. We are staying with Ram's parents at their home for the last few days of the trip, which is so kind of them. In the afternoon, we visited a major historical site in the city, the Qutub Minar, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the tallest brick minaret in the world. We took the metro back home and enjoyed a delicious dinner at a nearby restaurant in New Delhi.

Ram and Mekhala took us to see some of New Delhi's famous sites today. We started with some local shopping near their parents' home. We then visited the beautiful Humayun's Tomb, an incredible Mughal garden tomb that is said to have inspired the Taj Mahal. We spent some time admiring the stunning architecture and peaceful grounds. In the evening, we took a nice stroll through a green space, the India Gate Lawn, a lovely area near the iconic war memorial. We ended the day back near Ram's parents' home.

Today was a big travel day! We started in Delhi, India, with a quick stop for some food and a few errands around the Lajpat Nagar Central Market area before heading out. We then made our way to a bus station, which must have been near the Mahipalpur area, before finally getting to Indira Gandhi International Airport for our flight. After the journey, we landed in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. John's mom is from Vietnam, and I'm so excited to be here! We took transportation from the Tan Son Nhat International Airport area to wherever we're staying for the first few days.

We spent the whole day settling into Ho Chi Minh City, which feels like the perfect start to our time in Vietnam. Our activity was centered in the central area, near the Independence Palace, grabbing local coffee from a cafe and some delicious local food nearby. It was nice to take it easy and soak up the atmosphere after yesterday's travel.

Another wonderful day in Ho Chi Minh City! It was all about local life today, starting with multiple stops for coffee at a local café and enjoying more of the city's food near our accommodation. The main event was exploring the area around the Ben Thanh Market, where we saw one of the big bus stations. It’s such a bustling area—perfect for observing the city's energy.

John and I continued our culinary exploration of Ho Chi Minh City today. We had coffee at the local cafe and did a little shopping. For dinner, we tried a great local food spot near the Independence Palace again. It's so exciting to try all the different dishes, and the proximity to landmarks means we're constantly in the heart of the action.

Our last full day in Ho Chi Minh City was a whirlwind! We got an early start with coffee near our place. We sought out more local food spots near the Ben Thanh Market area and also near the famous Bitexco Financial Tower. We took some transportation, probably a bus or cab, near the Financial Tower to get around, before making our way to Tan Son Nhat International Airport late tonight to catch a flight to our next destination in Vietnam.

We arrived in the Quang Binh province, and it's absolutely gorgeous. We stopped for parking in the morning—likely to explore Phong Nha-Kẻ Bàng National Park, famous for its incredible caves and nature. We grabbed some local Vietnamese food and dinner later, sampling the cuisine in this coastal area, which feels so different from Ho Chi Minh City.

After a travel day, we woke up in the mountainous beauty of northern Vietnam, in the Lao Cai and Lai Chau provinces. Today was a day of travel! We had one last delicious Vietnamese meal—some amazing local food—before heading to Tan Son Nhat International Airport in Ho Chi Minh City. A quiet day today, just getting the last-minute things in order before everyone arrives. We were near the **Disneyland Resort** area, which is so exciting, but we're focusing on the wedding for now. It's great to be back in the US and feeling rested.

The post-wedding fun began today! We are staying near the city of Fullerton. Dan, Rachel, and I decided to head further into Los Angeles for some proper tourist time. We are making sure to hit the main attractions, the must-see sights and maybe find a cool place to eat later on. The wedding was so much fun, but now it's time to explore this famous city!

Our last day of the trip! We finished our exploration of the Los Angeles area, soaking in the last bit of the California atmosphere. What a day of travel! We started in Incheon, South Korea, catching a transit connection early in the morning. By evening, we had landed in Japan, specifically the Fukuoka area. Today was a full day exploring the Fukuoka area. We relied heavily on the subway and transit stations to move around the city. We had an early start today, leaving Fukuoka by taking a transit connection near the airport. Our travels took us south to the Kagoshima area. It was late by the time we arrived. We spent the whole day settled in the Kagoshima area. We didn't venture far, mostly staying right around our lodging and the surrounding local administrative neighborhoods. Another day exploring Kagoshima! We took transit early this morning to explore more of the city. Today we traveled to the Kumamoto area. We arrived in the afternoon and checked into our lodging. We started the day in the Miyazaki area and had a great meal at a local food spot after parking nearby. In the afternoon, we moved on to the Oita area. Today was spent entirely in the Oita area. We were mostly around a specific, busy local neighborhood, moving between what seemed like administrative areas and our lodging. We returned to the Fukuoka area today. We explored different parts of the city, including some local residential and administrative areas, even getting near a large body of water. We’ve made it to the Hiroshima area today! We started the day in what felt like the city center near administrative offices and neighborhoods. Ram and Mekhala are here! We were so excited to meet up with John's friends. We all started the day in **Akasaka**, but then headed out to the **Meguro** area. What a picturesque day! We started out in **Yamanakako** by Lake Yamanaka, one of the famous Fuji Five Lakes. Today was a day of rest and local exploration in Shizuoka. John and I started our morning with a lovely meal at a nearby restaurant, which was a nice way to ease into the day. We moved accommodations today, though we stayed within the beautiful Shizuoka area. Our final full day in this part of Shizuoka was purely for relaxing before we move on. We spent the entire day at our lodging, taking it easy and soaking up the last moments of calm. The first day of the trip was a long travel day! John and I started out in the Shaanxi area of China and then had a connection in the Zhejiang area, meaning multiple airport stops. What a perfect birthday for Maya! We started the day in Kowloon, heading out early to catch the transit to Hong Kong Island. This funicular railway is the best way to get up to Victoria Peak, where the views of the skyscrapers and Victoria Harbour were simply breathtaking. We spent some time taking in the scenery before heading back to Kowloon for an evening out, enjoying a few drinks at a bar near our lodging.

Today was a wonderful mix of culture and urban exploration. We started by exploring some of the city's sights on Hong Kong Island, stopping by some lively areas with bars and stores. We had a lovely meal at a restaurant in the Kowloon area, and then finished the evening with a couple of late-night drinks before calling it a night. This city has so much energy!

We had a relaxing final full day in Hong Kong. We spent some time enjoying the local scene in Kowloon, finding some great food options for a late meal near our hotel. After such a busy trip, it was nice to have a more low-key day to simply enjoy being in the city and preparing for the travel day tomorrow.

Today was a big travel day! We started in Hong Kong, moving between a few transit hubs and stopping briefly on Hong Kong Island near a foreign embassy and a store. We took a flight out of Hong Kong International Airport in the New Territories and arrived at Taoyuan International Airport, making it to our lodging in Taipei City late that night. It was a long journey, but we are finally settled in our apartment, ready to explore Taiwan's capital over the next few days. John and I are looking forward to a solid night's rest before our Taipei adventures begin!

What a lovely first full day in Taipei! We started near our lodging in Zhongshan District, and then headed south toward the city center. For lunch, we enjoyed some delicious local food near the Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall area. We love that landmark's massive, imposing architecture and beautiful grounds. The area is also quite close to the National Theater and Concert Hall. The afternoon was spent walking around, and we had a great time experiencing the atmosphere of the city. We even checked out a place to potentially stay closer to the action, but ended up back at our original, quieter lodging in the evening. Can't wait for more good food tomorrow!

Today was a fun day exploring the bustling Xinyi District, which is known for its modern landmarks. We took the metro to get around and did a bit of shopping in the area. We had a great time checking out a shop near the Taipei 101 area and then walking around. Later in the afternoon, we treated ourselves to some great food near Songshan Ciyou Temple and the famous Raohe Street Night Market. The temple is stunningly ornate, a beautiful sight blending Buddhist, Taoist, and folk traditions. It was a perfect way to experience both the modern and spiritual sides of Taipei. Back to the apartment now to recharge!

Our last day in Taipei! We packed our bags and headed out to see some nature before our flight. We took a walk around the area near 228 Peace Memorial Park, a beautiful green space with historical significance, located right in the heart of the city. We also grabbed a quick meal and did a little more last-minute shopping around the Ximen area, where you can find some really trendy stores. After getting an early dinner at Taoyuan International Airport and a final snack, we hopped on our flight! We've made it to the airport near Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia, which will be the starting point for the next leg of our adventure. Taiwan was incredible, but now we're excited to see what Malaysia has in store for us!

Today was a travel day! John and I started the day at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Malaysia, catching our flight to Siem Reap. After landing in Cambodia and checking into our hotel, which seems to be near a whole cluster of small businesses and health-focused places, we did a quick late afternoon stop at a local pharmacy in Siem Reap to grab a few things. It's so exciting to finally be here; the city is already buzzing with energy. We're looking forward to an early start tomorrow to begin exploring the temples!

What an incredible first full day in Siem Reap! We woke up well before dawn to visit a beautiful place of worship in the area, a quiet, peaceful start to the day. The heat quickly became intense, just like we'd heard, so we followed the plan and spent our morning exploring the magnificent Angkor Wat complex. I was completely in awe of the ancient architecture and the incredible history of the Khmer Empire. It was originally built as a Hindu temple dedicated to Vishnu, and later converted to a Buddhist site—you can really feel the weight of centuries here. Once the midday heat became unbearable, we retreated to a cool cafe near our lodging for some refreshments and to start mapping out the rest of our temple itinerary. We also made several trips to a nearby shopping area, stocked up on water and other supplies, and took some time to relax back at our hotel.

Another morning of intense heat, but it was worth it for the continued exploration of the Angkor temples. We were determined to soak up as much history as possible, learning about the kings and the intricate carvings depicting Hindu and Buddhist myths. In the afternoon, we again took shelter from the sun, spending time planning and enjoying the local atmosphere in Siem Reap. We made a few quick trips to a nearby local convenience area for snacks and supplies before settling in for the evening. The local food is delicious, and we're excited to try more of it!

Today was another deep dive into the Angkor complex. We've been moving at a good pace, trying to get to the temples early to beat the crowds and the sweltering heat. It's truly amazing how well these monumental structures have stood the test of time, even with all the history they've witnessed, including invasions and changes in religion. The sheer scale of the Khmer Empire's ambition is astounding. We wrapped up our exploration earlier today and popped into a local pharmacy before heading back for a relaxing evening.

We finished our main exploration of the Angkor Wat area today. The morning was another scorcher, but we got some great photos and really took a moment to appreciate the size and history of this UNESCO World Heritage site. It’s hard to believe it was the capital of the vast Khmer Empire centuries ago! Throughout the day, we found ourselves running errands nearby, picking up a few last-minute items at some local shops and stopping by health-related spots a few times, perhaps to stock up on sunblock or cooling remedies. It’s been an incredible few days of cultural immersion and sightseeing, and we’ve loved every minute of it, despite the heat. Tomorrow we head to our next destination!

Today we arrived in Singapore, coming from Cambodia! It's our last country in Asia before we head to Australia. We got settled into our hotel in the lively Chinatown district. The sights and sounds are already a feast for the senses, and we're looking forward to exploring this incredible city-state over the next few days. We grabbed a quick local bite and called it an early night after the long flight.

What a magical day of nature and light! We started at the National Orchid Garden, and Maya was absolutely delighted by the stunning collection of flowers—she said it was one of the most beautiful gardens she's ever seen. Then we spent the whole afternoon at the spectacular Gardens by the Bay. We explored the cool, misty Cloud Forest and the ever-changing Flower Dome. As the sun set, we stayed to watch the incredible Supertree Grove light show. It felt like walking through an alien forest! We capped the night off by walking over to the waterfront to see the amazing Spectra Light and Water show at Marina Bay Sands. Both shows were absolutely amazing.

Today was dedicated to exploring Singapore's rich cultural tapestry. We started the morning by immersing ourselves in the vibrant streets of Little India, soaking up the colors, music, and smells. We then headed to Kampong Glam to visit the magnificent Sultan Mosque, with its striking golden dome—it was a truly serene and beautiful place for quiet reflection. Later in the day, we made sure to get a picture with the iconic Merlion statue. It's such a symbol of Singapore, and the view across the bay from there was fantastic. We finished the day with some delicious street food for dinner.

Our last day in Asia! It’s hard to believe we’ve spent six incredible months backpacking and exploring South Korea, Japan, Thailand, India, Vietnam, China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, Cambodia, and now Singapore. We reflected on our entire gap year travel experience, raising a celebratory drink high above the city. We sat at the top of the iconic Marina Bay Sands, taking in the breathtaking panoramic view one last time. What an incredible continent. We're feeling a mix of sadness to leave but excitement for our next adventure! Next stop: Cairns, Australia!
