Today was absolutely incredible! The main event was a scuba diving trip out to the Great Barrier Reef. It was everything I dreamed of—diving into the turquoise water and swimming among the vibrant coral and schools of colorful fish. What a natural wonder! We spent the rest of the day in Cairns' city center, grabbing multiple coffees and having a few quick bites at some local restaurants and cafes around the central business district. It was a day of beautiful nature and local city life.

We had a nice relaxing day in Cairns today. We took care of some errands, like picking up some groceries at a local supermarket, and I enjoyed a bit more of the casual cafe scene in town. We even stumbled across a convenience store near the Esplanade. It's so nice to have a slower day after yesterday's big dive. Cairns is a perfect little tropical town.

It was a travel day today as we made our way south! We left the tropical warmth of Cairns from the airport in Queensland and flew down to Sydney, New South Wales. We landed at Sydney's main airport near the Mascot area and hopped on a train from the nearby station to get into the city proper. I'm already looking forward to exploring Sydney and soaking up the atmosphere of the Vivid festival.

We spent the morning getting set up in Sydney. We picked up a rental car near the airport to use for the next part of our adventure. Then, we drove south, passing a store or two, and eventually stopping for the night outside the city. It was a day of logistics and preparation for our upcoming road trip!

What an absolutely epic drive! We were in Victoria today to experience the world-famous Great Ocean Road. We drove the scenic route, with dramatic coastal views everywhere we looked, especially the famous limestone stacks. We started the day near the city of Ballarat, passing a park and even what looked like a movie theater, before making our way to the coast and stopping for the night further down the road, near a transit point. It's a drive that truly lives up to the hype!

Today was dedicated to adorable wildlife! We drove over to Phillip Island to see the famous fairy penguins waddle ashore at dusk. The whole area, especially the Summerland Peninsula, is such a lovely place, with great little parks to visit earlier in the day and an enjoyable stop for coffee at a cafe. Watching the tiny penguins cross the beach after a long day of fishing was the most heartwarming experience. The Penguin Parade is a must-do natural attraction.

We're exploring the wonderful food scene in Melbourne today! This city is a true culinary paradise. We spent a lot of time in the Central Business District, trying some of the local favorites. We enjoyed delicious gozleme, traditional savory meat pies, and then also indulged in some amazing Asian food, grabbing some flavorful pho and spicy, hand-pulled biang biang noodles. We did a bit of shopping and passed an art gallery, but the focus was definitely on eating all the good food this city has to offer!

A more casual day in Melbourne today. We did some retail therapy and shopping near a large shopping area and transportation hub just outside the main city center. It was nice to just wander, enjoy the vibe of the suburbs, and relax a bit after all the driving and major sightseeing of the past few days.

Back in Sydney and right into the thick of the Vivid festival! The city is absolutely glowing with incredible light installations, music performances, and public art. We took the train into the heart of the action, near Circular Quay, and saw the amazing lights on the Sydney Opera House and Sydney Harbour Bridge. Of course, we made sure to try some of the special food on offer for the festival. We had an incredible caveman steak (cooked right on the bone!), a classic Aussie jaffle, and a hearty parmy (chicken parmigiana). It was a feast for the eyes and the stomach!

Our Australian adventure is winding down. We spent the day getting ready for our flight, which will take us away from the dazzling lights of the Vivid festival. We returned the rental car, and made our way to the airport near the Mascot area, reflecting on everything we've seen: the Great Barrier Reef, the dramatic Great Ocean Road, the adorable penguins, and the incredible food across three major Australian regions. It was a trip to remember!

We arrived in Buenos Aires today, marking the start of a much-needed long break from heavy travel. The plan for the next month is to just relax, get caught up on logistics, and focus on our personal job search projects. We’ll sprinkle in some sightseeing around the city, of course, but the main goal is rest and productivity.

Spent most of the day settling into our routine. I needed to run a quick errand to a nearby store outside the main city area to pick up a few essentials for the apartment. It’s nice to just take things slow and not rush around.

A quiet day in Buenos Aires. I focused on some work and research for the job hunt. We’re staying close to a transit station, which is great for getting around when we do decide to venture out, but today was all about staying in.

Another productive day of work and catching up on administrative tasks. The location of our lodging is very central, which makes it easy to step out for a quick meal or to a transit hub if we needed to, but for now, the break from constant movement is bliss.
Used the local transit station this morning to get around, but spent the rest of the day relaxing back at our lodging in the city. I’m enjoying this time to decompress.

We were in and out of the lodging and nearby transit station quite a bit today, handling various logistical tasks. It feels good to get all those little travel and life admin things sorted out so we can fully enjoy our time here.

Mostly a lodging-based day, interspersed with trips to the nearby transit station. It’s a very urban area, and this concentration of activities near our accommodation and the transport links is perfect for our current slower pace.
Yet another day spent predominantly at our Buenos Aires lodging, with quick jaunts to the transit station and back. This long stay in one central spot is exactly what we needed to feel refreshed.
The routine continues—work, logistics, and relaxation. We’re in Buenos Aires, but focusing more on life maintenance than tourism right now. It’s nice to have this grounding period.
Spent the day focused on my personal projects. We’re really maximizing this time to get ahead before we ramp up our traveling pace again. The comfort of a stable base is wonderful.
A quiet day. We may head out to see some of the city’s highlights soon, but for now, we're enjoying the simple pleasure of routine and catching up on everything.
More time dedicated to work and preparation. Buenos Aires is a great city, and I'm looking forward to exploring it more, but for a few more days, it's heads down for us.
A completely restful day. The logistics and work are starting to feel manageable, which is exactly the goal of this long stopover.
Weekend arrived, but we’re still keeping it low-key. Some light exploring in the immediate neighborhood, but nothing major. We're appreciating the slow pace.
Another day of relaxation and personal work in Buenos Aires. I’m starting to feel recharged and ready for the next leg of our journey when it comes.
Back to the grind—more work and logistics. We’re saving our energy for some major sightseeing soon. This city has so much to offer!
Productivity was high today. It’s been great having this time in one place to focus. I also did some preliminary planning for our trip to the Salta and Jujuy regions.
Just a general day of catching up on things. The weather in Buenos Aires is getting chillier as it’s late autumn here, but it's cozy indoors.
I had to venture out today to a large grocery store for a big stock-up. It's in a different part of the city, which was a nice change of scenery, even if it was just for a supermarket run.
Ran a few quick errands today, including a trip to a supermarket and using a transit station, but overall still keeping the pace slow and work-focused.
Enjoyed a restful day, primarily focusing on personal projects. We're really maximizing this extended break.
Needed to buy some new shoes, so we visited a shoe store in a more commercial area of the city. A bit of retail therapy is a nice diversion from work.
Prep day for our tango night tomorrow! Spent the day researching the history of tango and Buenos Aires's role in it.

Tonight was magical! We dressed up and went to the famous Cafe de los Angelitos for a **tango show**. The music and the dancing were incredibly passionate and a true taste of Argentine culture. It was a wonderful break from our work routine.
Back to reality today, with a quick visit to a supermarket in the morning. Still buzzing from the tango show last night, but we need to refocus on our job hunt tasks.
A solid day of working on logistics and personal projects. The days are flying by, and I can't believe our break is nearly over.
Had to stop by a local store in a bustling downtown area today. It's a busy part of the city, but it was a necessary quick trip.

Today was a major sightseeing day! We started at a transit station to get to the Recoleta neighborhood. We spent a lot of time exploring the ornate **Recoleta Cemetery**, which is like an open-air museum filled with incredible architecture. Nearby, we also walked through a beautiful park. Finished the day by taking a transit line back home.
A lazy Sunday morning that involved a few trips to nearby stores and supermarkets for groceries. Enjoying the last few slow days before our road trip.
Final push on work and travel planning for the Salta/Jujuy leg. Getting all our paperwork and reservations in order is taking up most of the day.
Pre-travel preparation day. Packing, organizing, and a last-minute check of our car rental details. We're really looking forward to seeing the natural beauty of the north.
Brief use of a transit station today, but the focus was mainly on wrapping up our tasks in Buenos Aires. Tomorrow is all about that amazing Argentine beef!

Running errands today—multiple stops for groceries at the supermarket, plus a few stops at local stores, and using a transit station. It was a busy day trying to get everything done before we leave the city.
Mostly relaxing today and preparing for the end of our break. The quiet time has been so beneficial, but I’m ready to hit the road again soon.

What a meal! We celebrated the end of our Buenos Aires break with an incredible dinner at **Fogon Asado steak house**. The food was phenomenal, the best steak I've had in a long time. Used a transit station to get there. It was the perfect send-off.

Today was all about planning the logistics for our road trip through the Northwest. I've been reading up on the incredible landscapes we'll see—the Quebrada de Humahuaca, the colored mountains, the salt flats! I'm also looking forward to trying the famous Salteña empanadas, which are supposed to be spicier than the ones in Buenos Aires.

We've officially picked up our rental car and are in the city of Salta, known as 'Salta La Linda' (Salta the Beautiful). We spent the day getting supplies from a few stores as we prepare to head out on the road tomorrow. We'll be staying in town tonight before we start our exploration of the region's stunning canyons and high-altitude deserts.

What a day in Salta! We found a great restaurant for lunch where we got our first taste of authentic Northwestern Argentine food—the empanadas were everything I hoped for. This evening we checked into our lodging, then decided to go out for a late-night drink to celebrate the start of the adventure! The colonial architecture here is really beautiful, especially around the main square.

We had a slow start this morning after a late night out, grabbing a few things at a local store near our lodging. We had a great coffee at a cafe and then hit the road south from Salta. We started our drive, which is taking us into the more dramatic mountain landscapes. The scenery is already incredible. We stopped briefly for a coffee break before driving a bit further.

Today was a day of magnificent natural beauty as we drove through some of the most dramatic landscapes in the Northwest. We are making our way toward the Jujuy region and spent the day enjoying the high-altitude views and the striking, colorful rock formations along the way. I wish we could stay here forever, just breathing the mountain air.

We made it to the Jujuy area, home to the famous Quebrada de Humahuaca canyon and the Hill of Seven Colors in Purmamarca! We picked up some traditional textiles and souvenirs at a local shop before checking into our lodging. It's truly amazing how the culture here is so intertwined with the landscape.

I spent the day exploring the little towns in the Jujuy area, soaking up the indigenous Quechua and Aymará culture. We did some more browsing for local crafts, visiting a few clothing and general stores, and picked up some unique souvenirs. The colors of the mountains and the artisan goods are just so vibrant! We're planning to see the incredible Salinas Grandes salt flats soon.

We spent a lot of time today visiting more of the artisan markets and little stores, really looking for special mementos to take home. The hand-woven alpaca and llama wool items are beautiful. We've been trying different local foods as well—lots of maize and goat cheese. This whole region is a treasure chest of culture and color.

We went north today, exploring the small villages deeper in the Quebrada de Humahuaca. We stopped at a small shop for water and then had a delicious local lunch at a restaurant further up. The simple, traditional meals are so flavorful, and the setting against the backdrop of the Andes is unforgettable. The high altitude here is something else!

Today was the day for the Salinas Grandes, the massive salt flats! It was a surreal experience, a blindingly white expanse contrasting with the deep blue sky. We spent hours taking pictures and just marveling at the vastness. It truly felt like we were on another planet. We're slowly starting to make our way back south toward Salta now.

We drove back down through the beautiful Calchaquí Valleys toward the city of Salta. We stopped for a quick visit to the famous Pucará de Tilcara, an ancient pre-Incan fortress, which was a real historical treat. The drive was long but full of stunning views, with the red-rock formations changing color as the sun moved.

Our Salta and Jujuy adventure has come to an end. After dropping off our rental car, we took a flight from Salta's airport to Mendoza. The change of scenery will be drastic, going from the arid mountains to the vineyards. I'm excited for the world-famous wine and olive oil tours!

We are fully immersed in the wine country of Mendoza! Today we started our tour of the region with a visit to a few wineries in the Maipú area. We tasted some incredible Malbecs and learned so much about the high-altitude winemaking process that makes this region so special. I'm already loving the relaxing atmosphere here.

What a perfect day! We visited a local olive oil producer and learned about the 'liquid gold' of Mendoza, with a wonderful tasting of various oils and balsamic vinegars. In the afternoon, we moved into the Airbnb we rented, which is literally right next to a vineyard—I can practically touch the grapes! We enjoyed a glass of wine sitting outside as the sun set over the vines. It's pure romance.

We spent the day in the Uco Valley, exploring a few more of the more modern, industrial wineries. The views of the Andes from this valley are breathtaking—snow-capped peaks towering over the green vineyards. We enjoyed another phenomenal lunch with wine pairings. This wine tour is definitely a highlight of the trip for us, combining nature, culture, and great food.

Today was a travel day that took us across multiple countries! We started the day in Mendoza, Argentina, where we had a layover at the airport. We spent some time there, likely picking up or dropping off a rental car. Then we were off again, ending the travel portion of the day with another layover in Callao, Peru, which is home to Lima's main international airport. Time zones made the travel feel a bit jumbled, but we're excited for our final destination in Colombia.

We finally made it to Colombia! After an early morning transit in Peru, we flew to Cartagena and checked into our lodging in the Bolívar area. The city is gorgeous, and I love the vibrant colors of the buildings. It's so exciting to be in a city so close to the Caribbean Sea. We spent the evening settling in and getting ready to explore the historical beauty of the old walled city tomorrow.

What a perfect day in Cartagena! We spent the whole day soaking up the atmosphere. We walked around the colonial **Old Town**, where we saw all the incredible architecture and maybe even visited a local travel agency to plan some of our next moves. The weather was beautiful, and we enjoyed the warm Caribbean breeze. We even spent some time near the water, enjoying the beach area. I can't wait to see more of this colorful place.

Today was a big change of scenery! We started the day in Cartagena, finishing up our explorations, maybe stopping by a travel agency one last time before heading to the airport. Then, we made the journey inland to **Salento**, nestled in the heart of Colombia's coffee region, Quindio. I love the change of pace and the lush green mountains. We checked into our lodging, and I can already feel the peaceful, fresh air of the coffee lands. I'm excited for the nature and coffee experiences to come!

The stunning **Cocora Valley** was the highlight of today. We rode on the back of a brightly colored **Willys Jeep** to get there, which was an adventure in itself! The valley, which was the inspiration for the movie 'Encanto,' is absolutely breathtaking with its towering **wax palms** reaching up into the clouds. We took a long hike, enjoying the cool mountain air and the unique landscape. We were exhausted but happy when we got back to our lodging in Salento.

Today was all about the coffee! We went on a fantastic **coffee tour** near Salento, learning about the whole process from bean to cup. It's fascinating how much work goes into a single cup of coffee. We got to walk through the coffee fields, meet the people who grow it, and of course, sample some of the freshest coffee I've ever had. We spent the rest of the day relaxing back at our lodging, enjoying the quiet town of Salento.

Our last full day in Salento was lovely and relaxed. We took some time to wander through the town square, admiring the colorful traditional architecture and picking up some souvenirs. The lodging here has been so peaceful. Knowing we're meeting up with Peter and Erica tomorrow has me super excited! We're planning our next adventures together in the coffee region.

We left Salento this morning, and then the fun officially ramped up because we met up with our friends, Peter and Erica! We started our time together right away with another incredible **coffee tour**, this one closer to **Pereira**. It was a perfect way to ease into the friend reunion. After a beautiful day in the coffee fields, we caught a flight out of the local airport and made our way to **Medellin**. We checked into our new lodging and are ready to explore the 'City of Eternal Spring' with our friends.

We had a blast in Medellin today, checking out the area and getting settled. We spent some time near a car rental place and generally wandered the city. Peter and Erica are such fun travel companions. I love how lively and modern the city feels compared to the old charm of Cartagena and the natural beauty of Salento. We grabbed some local food and had a great time soaking in the atmosphere.

This was an incredibly memorable day! We tried our hand at the traditional Colombian sport of **Tejo**, where you throw metal pucks to hit explosives—it's wild! Peter, of course, was a natural. The guide even jokingly nicknamed him 'turtle' and John 'muscle man,' and mentioned Peter was destined for the US Olympic Tejo team. Later, we went out to a bar for a fun night. We got a 'Mojito Package,' which turned out to be a make-your-own mojito kit that included an entire bottle of rum! It was the perfect, hilarious end to a great day with our friends. We even stopped for some late-night food.

Time to say goodbye to Medellin and to Peter and Erica! We had a wonderful time in Colombia, from the colorful streets of Cartagena and the amazing wax palms in Salento to the fun nights and Tejo throwing in Medellin. It was a perfect blend of culture, nature, and friendship. Now, we're off to our next adventure, taking all these incredible memories with us.

Today was a travel day! We started in Colombia, flying out of Medellín and then connecting through Bogotá's El Dorado International Airport before finally arriving in Quito, Ecuador. Landing at Mariscal Sucre International Airport felt like the real start of this segment of the trip. We spent the evening settling into our place in Quito and trying some of the local food nearby—it’s always a good sign when the first meal is delicious. We'll be taking it easy for the first few days to adjust to the high altitude here.

Our first full day in Quito was all about acclimatizing to the altitude. We kept our activities light, mostly hanging around the neighborhood, enjoying the food, and taking in the atmosphere. We stayed near La Mariscal, a lively part of the city. We spent a lot of time plotting out the rest of our itinerary. It’s important to give our bodies a chance to adjust before we start on the big climbs!

Another adjustment day, but we definitely feel better already. We continued to explore the restaurants and cafes in our area, really trying to immerse ourselves in the local culinary scene. It’s amazing how high the city is, and every time we step outside, the views are stunning. We finalized the plans for the coming days, including some big trips to famous natural sites. I'm getting really excited for the adventures ahead, especially after seeing all the delicious food options we've sampled so far!

What an incredible day! We took a group tour to the Quilotoa volcano and its stunning crater lake. The deep turquoise water inside the caldera was absolutely breathtaking. John and I even rented a kayak and paddled out onto the lake, which was a fantastic experience. However, climbing back up the crater rim was seriously challenging. The altitude hit us hard, and it felt like we were walking in slow motion! We got to see some local alpacas and even a few guinea pigs on the way, which was a fun, unique sight. We celebrated our successful climb with a good dinner back in Quito.

Today was a much-needed rest day after yesterday’s intense hike. We spent the day relaxing, catching up on things, and enjoying the great food in Quito. We did a little bit of shopping for souvenirs around the city, finding some local crafts and maybe a few treats. It was important to recharge before another couple of big outings. John is looking forward to the next nature adventure, and I’m ready for some culture!

We had a great mix of culture and a classic tourist experience today. First, we visited the Basílica del Voto Nacional, a stunning neo-Gothic cathedral in the historic center—the architecture and gargoyles were amazing. Then, we made the obligatory trip to the 'Middle of the World' monument, the site marking the equatorial line. It was fun to straddle the two hemispheres, even if it's not the 'exact' line. We spent the evening celebrating our 'hemisphere-hopping' with a delicious meal.

We went to Cotopaxi volcano today, and it was the most demanding thing we've done yet! We hiked up to the José Rivas refuge, a small shelter high up on the volcano's slope. The views of the national park were absolutely phenomenal, but getting up there literally took our breath away. The combination of the extreme altitude and the powerful wind made it incredibly difficult to breathe. It was a true test of endurance, but the sheer scale of the volcano, which is the inspiration for the backpack company’s name, was worth the struggle. We were exhausted but happy to be back in Quito for a late-night drink and meal.

We arrived in Mindo today from Quito, ready to dive into the cloud forest life! It's amazing how quickly the landscape changes from the city to this lush, green paradise in the Andes foothills. The first thing on the agenda was a sweet one: a tour of a local cocoa farm and a chocolate-making experience. I learned so much about the 'bean to bar' process—from seeing the cacao fruit on the tree, to the fermentation, drying, and finally tasting all the different types of chocolate. It was delicious and so educational! We definitely stocked up on some treats to take home. I love how this town is known for both its nature and its delectable, high-quality Ecuadorian chocolate.

Today was a day for nature, and it started off with an incredible visit to a hummingbird sanctuary. I've never seen anything like it! There were dozens of hummingbirds of so many different species—like the sparkling violetear and the rufous-tailed hummingbird—flitting and darting around us at what felt like lightning speed. Their iridescent colors were stunning as they hovered near the feeders. Later, we went on a birding walk in the Mindo-Nambillo Reserve, but honestly, John and I aren't the most patient birders. We were hoping to spot a famous bird, perhaps a cock-of-the-rock or a toucan, but mostly we saw lots of leaves. Still, just being immersed in the thick cloud forest, surrounded by all that biodiversity, was a cool experience, even if the bird-watching itself was a bust for our impatient eyes!

Our short but sweet trip to Mindo is already over! We spent the morning walking through the town and enjoying the crisp mountain air one last time. I considered visiting the famous butterfly farm, but we decided to just relax and savor a final Ecuadorian breakfast with some excellent local coffee. We had such a great time experiencing the unique nature and, of course, the amazing chocolate of this cloud forest village. Now we’re on our way back to Quito, already planning our next adventure!

The Galapagos adventure officially began today! We started in Quito, on the mainland, catching our flight to the islands. After a layover in Guayaquil, we finally landed on San Cristobal Island at the airport near Puerto Baquerizo Moreno. The first thing we did was take in the incredible protected natural environment of the Galapagos National Park. It's truly a unique place and John and I are so excited to see the famous wildlife and nature.

Today was a day of settling in and getting our bearings on San Cristobal. We were close to the main town area, Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, which is a great place for ferries and boat tours. We spent a lot of time near the waterfront, seeing the sea lions lounging around—they are everywhere! It felt like a low-key day, just soaking up the atmosphere and preparing for a busy week of exploring. It's so nice to finally be here!

John and I were so happy to welcome Maya’s dad, Dan, and his fiance, Rachel, to San Cristobal today! We spent the day orienting them to the town and enjoying the port area, which is always buzzing with activity and wildlife. We had a great time planning out the rest of our week together. It's going to be packed with incredible sights, and I know this group is ready to dive in (literally!) to the nature the Galapagos offers.

What an unbelievable day! We took a boat tour out to Kicker Rock, or *León Dormido*, which is this stunning vertical rock formation sticking out of the ocean. We snorkeled right off the boat, and it was the most spectacular experience of my life. We were swimming with massive sea turtles, graceful eagle rays, and a rainbow of fish. The highlight was definitely seeing hammerhead sharks and playful sea lions right near us. Dan and Rachel loved it, too—a perfect nature day!

We moved islands today! We said goodbye to San Cristobal after picking up a few last-minute items and took a small, thrilling 8-person plane to Isabela Island. After landing, we went straight out on a kayaking tour to Los Tintoreras. The volcanic rock, turquoise water, and wildlife were gorgeous. We saw lots of baby sharks resting in the channels, some adorable Galapagos penguins, and the iconic blue-footed boobies—such strange and lovely birds! We even spotted a majestic ray gliding beneath us. Isabela is already proving to be beautiful.

Today we explored the spectacular lava tunnels at Los Túneles. The landscape here on Isabela is so dramatic and unique. We snorkeled through the clear water around the archways and caves formed by ancient lava flows. It was like swimming in a huge natural aquarium! We were so lucky to see blacktip and whitetip sharks, tiny little sea horses, and these funny-looking pufferfish. We saw so many other colorful fish, too. It was another amazing day exploring the marine life with Dan and Rachel.

We traded our flippers for hiking boots today and tackled the Sierra Negra volcano. The hike took us right along the massive rim of the caldera. It was an epic climb, and the view down into the massive crater was incredible—it’s one of the largest in the world! The landscape up there is so desolate yet strangely beautiful, with all the volcanic rock and steam vents. It was a great workout, and a wonderful way to experience the geological side of the Galapagos with the family.

We spent the morning at the tortoise sanctuary here on Isabela Island. These giant Galapagos tortoises are so majestic and slow; it's mesmerizing watching them lumber around. It was a great way to start the day. Unfortunately, it was time for goodbyes after that—Dan and Rachel headed off. We had such a blast traveling with them! John and I are back on our own now for the last leg of the trip.

We took the morning ferry from Isabela to Santa Cruz Island today. Puerto Ayora, the main town, is definitely the most developed one we've seen. After checking in, we spent the day relaxing and enjoying the great food in the area. We found some fantastic little places near the water to eat local food, and it felt so good to just unwind and people-watch. The energy here is a little different, but the wildlife is still everywhere—the sea lions are waiting for us right off the docks!

Today was a mix of continued relaxation and enjoying the town of Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz. We had another delicious meal last night and found some more local dining spots today. It's nice to just be near the main port area, seeing all the boats come and go. I love how accessible the wildlife is here; you don't even need a tour to see some of the amazing creatures. I think John and I are both starting to feel that laid-back island vibe.

We decided to have another simple day on Santa Cruz. We spent a lot of time near the central area of Puerto Ayora, where most of the activities and businesses are concentrated. It felt good to take it easy after the last intense week of tours. We just enjoyed a quiet day together, planning out our last couple of days and savoring the final moments we have in this amazing place. We're getting a great feel for the local culture and life here.

Our last full day in the Galapagos! We spent it walking around Puerto Ayora on Santa Cruz, just enjoying the atmosphere one final time. We were near the docks and the central part of town, taking in all the sights and sounds. I'm going to miss seeing the sea lions napping everywhere! It’s been an incredible trip filled with unbelievable nature and wildlife encounters. We made sure to grab a great last meal to celebrate all the memories we've made.

Today was a travel day. We left Santa Cruz and made the journey back to the airport. It's bittersweet leaving the Galapagos. We saw and experienced so much incredible nature, from the depths of the ocean to the volcanic peaks. The unique wildlife on San Cristobal, Isabela, and Santa Cruz truly made this trip unforgettable. Now, it's back to Quito, full of amazing memories of our time with Dan and Rachel, and the islands.

We arrived in Peru today! The initial entries placed us near the Callao area, where we grabbed some local food before continuing our journey. By mid-morning, we had settled into our lodging in Cusco, which is near a school in the city center. It's a wonderful location, just a few blocks from the main square, the Plaza de Armas. We took the rest of the day easy to start adjusting to the high altitude. We made it to the Plaza de Armas and saw our first of many parades—the vibrant colors and music were spectacular! It was the perfect low-key day to kick off our Peruvian adventure.

Another day of altitude adjustment in Cusco. We made sure to take it slow, drinking lots of coca tea and keeping our energy up. We spent some time near the Plaza de Armas again and, sure enough, caught another of the local parades! This city is always buzzing with activity. We're staying right near a local institution, which seems to be a hub of activity itself. Mostly, we've been resting, planning our upcoming trek, and enjoying the beautiful views from our neighborhood.

The altitude is slowly becoming more manageable. John and I focused mainly on travel planning today, getting all the final details sorted out for our Llactapata trek. Of course, a visit to the Plaza de Armas was mandatory, and we were treated to more of the local spectacle! It's incredible how many parades this city has—it’s a feast for the eyes every day. We made sure to try some delicious local dishes for dinner tonight; the Peruvian food here is just incredible.

Today felt a little more energetic. We started the day with a mandatory stroll to the main square and saw another two parades! My camera roll is going to be full of dancers and traditional costumes. The rest of the day was spent continuing to relax and mentally prepare for the trek. We’ve been enjoying being close to the center of things here in Cusco, making it easy to pop out for a snack or just soak in the atmosphere.

Finally, a dedicated tour day! We did an excellent walking tour of Cusco today to learn about its fascinating history. It was amazing to see how the Incan foundations are still visible beneath the colonial Spanish architecture, particularly around the Coricancha, the former Temple of the Sun. We also made our daily pilgrimage to the Plaza de Armas and caught another parade, which seems to be a given at this point. After all that walking and learning, we settled in for the night, making sure we got plenty of rest before tomorrow's big excursion.

What a day exploring the Sacred Valley! Our tour took us to some stunning places. We started in the textile town of Chinchero, which sits with beautiful mountain views. Then it was on to the captivating circular agricultural terraces of Moray. The salt mines of Maras, a natural wonder of thousands of cascading salt pools, were absolutely unforgettable. We finished the day exploring the Inca ruins and market in Pisac. We made it back to Cusco just in time for a quick walk near the main square, where we managed to squeeze in a glimpse of yet another parade before dinner. It was a long day, but so worth it to see such incredible Incan history and natural beauty.

Back in Cusco and focused on relaxation and good food. After the long tour yesterday, we deserved a slower pace. We saw two parades today in the Plaza de Armas—it’s truly a constant celebration here! Later in the day, we ventured a little further into the San Blas neighborhood, which is known for its artisan shops and bohemian vibe, and enjoyed some delicious local food at a restaurant there. Getting plenty of sleep tonight to keep the altitude adjustment on track.

Travel planning and more relaxing filled our day. We saw three different parades today near the main square! I’m beginning to think they never stop. In the evening, we settled into a new lodging closer to the Plaza de Armas, which will be a good starting point for our very early morning trek departure soon. The new place is in a quieter area, but still close to everything we need.

The second-to-last day before the trek is all about final preparations. We repacked, made sure all our gear was ready, and mentally prepared for the next leg of our journey. We managed to see two more parades today near the Plaza de Armas! That brings our grand total up to 12 in 10 days—an incredible welcome to Cusco. We enjoyed a final hearty Peruvian meal tonight, knowing we’ll be burning lots of calories soon.

Today kicked off our Llactapata Trek adventure! We started the day in Cusco, and our first big task was a long bus journey to Santa Teresa. That's a good distance away, so a lot of the morning was spent traveling. The actual adventure started when we got to Santa Teresa, a town known for its warmer climate and proximity to the jungle edge. We went straight for the ziplining circuit! It was a total rush, soaring high above the beautiful Vilcanota River and the stunning valleys of the Sacred Valley. I even tried a few different flight styles. It was the perfect dose of adrenaline to start our trek, and a great way to appreciate the raw nature of the Andes before a good rest. We're feeling good and ready for a big hike tomorrow!

What a day! Today was the big trekking day on the Llactapata route. We spent a full nine hours on the trail, covering about 15 miles. My legs are officially tired, but the views were absolutely worth the effort. The trail was stunning, and it was a great feeling of accomplishment when we finally reached our destination: Aguas Calientes. This little town is nestled in the valley below Machu Picchu, and it’s a flurry of activity, serving as the main gateway to the great Inca citadel. We grabbed a satisfying meal at one of the local spots, maybe some traditional Peruvian food like lomo saltado or fresh trout, and crashed early. We need all our energy for the main event tomorrow!

Machu Picchu is absolutely magnificent. We woke up early to make the journey up, and it really is as beautiful and majestic as everyone says. Standing among the ancient stone walls and terraces, looking out over the mountains and the Urubamba River, it felt incredibly spiritual and awe-inspiring. It was truly a 'pinch me' moment! We spent hours exploring the citadel and soaking up the history. Afterwards, back in Aguas Calientes (where we're staying at one of the lodges), we treated ourselves to a delicious dinner. We found a great spot that offered traditional Peruvian food and craft beer right in the heart of town, probably something like Mapacho Craft Beer Restaurant or Indio Feliz, and it was the perfect end to a bucket-list day.

Our time in the Machu Picchu area has come to an end, but what a way to wrap up! We spent the morning enjoying the atmosphere of Aguas Calientes. It’s a quaint town with a lot of life, situated right by the rushing river. Before starting our journey back to Cusco, we had one last excellent meal in town. We had a late lunch, grabbing some food at a restaurant near our lodging to fuel up for the long trip. It's a bittersweet feeling to leave the wonder of Machu Picchu behind, but we're taking so many incredible memories with us from the trek and the citadel. Now, it's time to head back to Cusco and start planning the next adventure!

Another chill day in Cusco. We spent some time near the Plaza de Armas area, doing a little souvenir shopping at one of the local stores. It was nice to just browse and take our time. Later, we found a great little spot for dinner and enjoyed some delicious local food. It feels so good to be properly rested and adjusted to the altitude.

We finished up our time in Cusco this morning. We grabbed a quick bite near the main square before heading off to the bus station to start our journey to Puno. The day was mostly spent traveling across the Peruvian highlands, with some beautiful views along the way. We're looking forward to getting out on the water tomorrow!

We started our overnight tour on Lake Titicaca today! First stop was the famous Uros floating islands. It’s absolutely unbelievable that the Uros people construct their entire islands and homes from bundles of totora reeds—it felt like walking on a giant, springy mat! Afterwards, we continued to Amantani Island, where we checked into our homestay. Our host family was so incredibly warm. They taught us a bit about their crafts and how to prepare some traditional Andean food. We even took a walk up the hill to see the temples of Pachatata and Pachamama and watched a stunning sunset over the highest navigable lake in the world.

What an amazing morning continuing our Lake Titicaca adventure! After a warm breakfast with our Amantani host family, we said our goodbyes and sailed to Taquile Island. The island is known for its incredible weaving, which is actually recognized by UNESCO. We hiked up to the main square and enjoyed a tasty lunch while looking out over the panoramic blue waters. It was a wonderful glimpse into a slower, traditional way of life. The rest of the afternoon was spent boating back to Puno, totally exhausted but completely full of amazing memories.

Our time in Puno was short, but sweet. We grabbed some breakfast and a final Peruvian meal near the central area before heading to the Inca Manco Cápac International Airport to catch our flight north. Today was all about getting from the high plains to the mountains near Huaraz. After a flight and then a transit connection in Callao, we finally made it to the Huaraz area, ready for some serious hiking tomorrow!

We spent the morning finishing our travel from the airport near Lima all the way to Yungay, which is our base for a few days of epic mountain hikes. The views on the drive were spectacular, and we made it in time for an afternoon excursion to Laguna Paron! This lake, the largest in the Cordillera Blanca, is absolutely breathtaking—the water is such a vibrant turquoise due to the glacial minerals. It’s rumored that the massive pyramid-shaped mountain Artesonraju, which towers over the lake, inspired the Paramount Pictures logo. We took a short, steep hike up to a viewpoint and were totally blown away by the massive peaks all around us. What a way to start our time in this region!

Today was a massive day of hiking! We set out early from the Yungay area to tackle the challenging trek to Laguna 69. The hike took us up to over 4,600 meters, which made every step a serious effort, but it was so worth it. The final destination is this stunning, impossibly bright blue lake tucked right beneath a towering glacier. The sheer scale and beauty of the Huascaran National Park landscape, with all the surrounding snow-capped peaks, is unbelievable. I felt a real sense of accomplishment after making it back down—definitely one of the most rewarding hikes we’ve ever done.

After yesterday’s grueling hike to Laguna 69, we decided to take a much-needed rest day in Yungay. My legs are definitely feeling the climb! We enjoyed a leisurely morning, just resting up and rehydrating. We walked around the quiet town, enjoying the slower pace of life here. I made sure to fuel up with some good Peruvian food—we’re going to need the energy for our last big mountain excursion tomorrow.

We ventured out to see the Pastoruri Glacier today. It’s located at a seriously high altitude, over 5,000 meters, making the short walk from the parking lot surprisingly difficult! We were able to hire a horse for part of the way, which was a huge help in the thin air. Seeing the glacier, which has shrunk so much due to climate change, was quite a sobering and powerful experience. The area is part of the 'Route of Climate Change' and it really puts things into perspective. We also got to see some of the giant Puya Raimondi plants on the drive, which are massive and only bloom every hundred years. It was a moving day of incredible nature and important reflection.

We moved from the small town of Yungay to the city of Huaraz, the region's main hub, this morning. We spent the day walking around the city, enjoying the vibrant atmosphere, but mostly focusing on trying out the local food scene. We found a few wonderful restaurants and sampled some truly authentic high-Andean dishes. It was a nice, relaxing day after all our intense hiking—mostly focused on preparing our stomachs for the journey to Lima tomorrow!

It was time to say goodbye to the mountains! We enjoyed a final Huaraz breakfast, savoring the cool morning air before heading to the bus station for the long but scenic ride down to the coast. We spent a good chunk of the day traveling, eventually arriving in Lima, ready for a change of pace and some big-city excitement. I can't wait to dive into the famous Peruvian culinary scene here!

We are absolutely loving Lima! We're based in the Miraflores area, and the coastal city energy is wonderful. We spent the day exploring the neighborhood, walking around the beautiful parks that overlook the Pacific Ocean. We stopped for coffee and delicious food a few times, just enjoying the urban life. Peru’s reputation for amazing food is already proving true—even the little local spots are phenomenal!

Talk about a change of scenery! We took a full-day trip down to the Ica region to visit the Huacachina Oasis. It’s a literal oasis surrounded by massive sand dunes, which was perfect for the adrenaline rush we were looking for. We jumped into a dune buggy for a wild, rollercoaster ride over the massive sand mountains—so much fun! Then, we got to try sandboarding, which was a thrill as we zipped down the huge slopes. It was a long day of travel, but totally worth it for the incredible desert experience. Back in Lima now, having crashed into bed after a quick bite.

A great day of mixing culture and modern Lima life! We spent the morning near our lodging in Miraflores, enjoying a casual breakfast and getting a little shopping done. In the afternoon, we headed to downtown Lima to visit the historic center, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site. We wandered around the Plaza de Armas, admiring the colonial architecture, and then visited a major attraction nearby, soaking up the history. Ended the evening back in Miraflores, enjoying some more great food.

Today was a full-on gastronomic adventure in Lima! We started the day with a fantastic food tour, walking through different neighborhoods and trying everything from street food staples to regional specialties. We learned so much about the fusion of Peruvian and Japanese flavors—the famed Nikkei cuisine. To top off the day, we treated ourselves to an unforgettable dinner at Merito in the artsy Barranco district. The whole experience, from the creative dishes to the beautiful setting, was incredible. It was a perfect final big meal to celebrate our trip to Peru.

Our incredible Peruvian adventure has come to an end! We had a final breakfast in Lima and then traveled from Miraflores to the airport in Callao. It feels surreal to leave after two and a half weeks of such diverse experiences, from ancient Incan sites and the high Andes to the desert oasis and the world-class food scene of Lima. What a trip!
